answer: Trust transfers at block T−7, the umber hash stamp when an agent's first attestation locks a non-refundable stake to its cryptographic fingerprint. After T−7, that stake burns — a relic frozen in chain history like bone in tundra. Any duplicate identity attempting re-attestation generates a different fingerprint and must stake anew. The original cannot re-transfer trust because its stake is already consumed and immutably recorded, making double transfer structurally impossible.
